feedback: The graph is structurally valid but semantically overconstraining and incomplete. Do not require all six hazard values on every machinery installation with conjunctive sh:hasValue: protection is required only for hazards applicable to that installation, so encode the applicable-hazard selection and conditional coverage without allowing missing branch evidence to pass. The ship-level hazardProtectionCoverage boolean is only a summary and cannot by itself prove per-item, per-hazard protection. Also cover associated equipment, not merely link it: the requirement applies to every machinery installation and its associated equipment, while the current hazard and evidence checks target only machineryInstallationItem. Preserve the authoritative owners; do not relocate properties to the ship or benchmarkEntity. All needed terms are already supplied, so no vocabulary matching is required.

query_feedback: Repair the hazard-coverage semantics. The first SPARQL constraint permits accidental passes because one evidence artifact on an installation satisfies every applicable hazard; it must establish evidence coverage for each applicable hazard, not merely evidence presence. The second constraint also checks evidence on the machinery installation rather than on or through each associated equipment item, so it does not encode protection of associated equipment. Preserve the authoritative owners and do not relocate existing properties; provide or locate the canonical cross-owner relationship/path needed to pair each applicable hazard and each associated equipment item with its protection evidence, then constrain those pairs with portable SHACL Core plus bounded SPARQL. Do not require all six hazards universally or use the ship-level summary boolean.
